decisions.choice: This verse is 21:1 in the Hebrew text, 20:45 in many Bibles
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text begins chapter 21 here, with the short oracle against the forest of the south (21:1-5). Many Bibles attach these five verses to chapter 20 as 20:45-49, so their 21:1-32 is 21:6-37 here. Open Word Bible follows the numbering of the Hebrew text it translates, and Ezekiel is cited by the Hebrew numbers. The words are the same; only the numbers differ.

decisions.choice: the formula as in Jeremiah
decisions.reason: "The word of the LORD came to me, saying" keeps the wording set for Jeremiah at each level, here and at verses 6, 13 and 23. The LORD's words that follow take no quotation marks, as in chapter 20.

source.text: בֶּן־אָדָ֗ם שִׂ֤ים פָּנֶ֨יךָ֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ תֵּימָ֔נָה וְהַטֵּ֖ף אֶל־דָּר֑וֹם וְהִנָּבֵ֛א אֶל־יַ֥עַר הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה נֶֽגֶב׃

records.literal_gloss: Son of man, set your face [the] way toward [the] south, and drip toward [the] south, and prophesy against [the] forest of the field, [the] Negev.

en.L: Son of man, set your face toward the south, and drip [words] against the south, and prophesy against the forest of the field of the Negev.
en.B: Son of man, turn to face the south. Preach against the south, and prophesy against the forest land of the Negev.
en.R: Son of man, turn toward the south. Speak out against the south. Prophesy against the forest of the Negev, the land to the south.

fr.L: Fils d’homme, tourne ta face en direction du sud, et fais couler [tes paroles] vers le midi, et prophétise contre la forêt de la campagne du Néguev.
fr.B: Fils d’homme, tourne ton regard vers le sud. Prêche contre le midi, et prophétise contre la forêt du pays du Néguev.
fr.R: Fils d’homme, tourne-toi vers le sud. Parle contre le sud. Prophétise contre la forêt du Néguev, la région du sud.

es.L: Hijo de hombre, pon tu rostro hacia el sur, y derrama [palabras] contra el sur, y profetiza contra el bosque del campo del Néguev.
es.B: Hijo de hombre, vuélvete de cara al sur. Predica contra el sur y profetiza contra la tierra boscosa del Néguev.
es.R: Hijo de hombre, vuélvete hacia el sur. Habla en contra del sur. Profetiza contra el bosque del Néguev, la tierra del sur.

decisions.choice: set your face toward: turn to face, as a sign of the message against it
decisions.reason: The prophet turns toward the place he speaks against; see the note at 6:2. The same command opens the explanation of this oracle in verse 7.

decisions.choice: three words for "south": the south, the southland, the Negev
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses three different words for the south. The last, the Negev, is the dry region in the south of Judah. Seen from Babylon, where Ezekiel lived, the invading army would come down on Judah from the north, so Judah and Jerusalem lie to the "south". Verse 7 explains the picture: the south is Jerusalem, and the forest is the land of Israel.

decisions.choice: drip words: preach, let words fall like drops
decisions.reason: The verb "to drip" is used of preaching, as in Amos 7:16 and Micah 2:6, 11.

decisions.choice: turn to face (B); turn toward (R); preach (B); speak out (R)
decisions.reason: "Set your face toward" follows the wording set for Ezekiel at each level. "Drip" is kept at Literal, with "words" supplied, as in Amos 7:16; Balanced and Readable say "preach" and "speak out". Readable explains that the Negev is the land to the south.

decisions.choice: pon tu rostro hacia (L); vuélvete de cara a (B); vuélvete hacia (R)
decisions.reason: Ezekiel's 'set your face toward' keeps one wording at each level through the book; L keeps the Hebrew picture, B and R say the gesture plainly.

decisions.choice: derrama [palabras] (L); predica (B); habla en contra (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb means to let drops fall; L keeps the picture with the bracketed object Spanish needs, B and R give the sense.

decisions.choice: *sim panekha* "tourne ta face vers" (L), "tourne ton regard vers" (B), "tourne-toi vers" (R), for the whole book
decisions.reason: The settled French wording of Ezekiel's gesture against those he prophesies to.

decisions.choice: the three words for the south: "le sud", "le midi", "le Néguev" (L, B); "le sud", "la région du sud" (R)
decisions.reason: French has two ordinary words for the south, so Literal and Balanced can keep three different words as the Hebrew does; "Néguev" as in French 1 Samuel 27:10.

source.text: וְאָֽמַרְתָּ֙ לְיַ֣עַר הַנֶּ֔גֶב שְׁמַ֖ע דְּבַר־יְהוָ֑ה כֹּֽה־אָמַ֣ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֡ה הִנְנִ֣י מַֽצִּית־בְּךָ֣׀אֵ֡שׁ וְאָכְלָ֣ה בְךָ֣ כָל־עֵֽץ־לַח֩ וְכָל־עֵ֨ץ יָבֵ֤שׁ לֹֽא־תִכְבֶּה֙ לַהֶ֣בֶת שַׁלְהֶ֔בֶת וְנִצְרְבוּ־בָ֥הּ כָּל־פָּנִ֖ים מִנֶּ֥גֶב צָפֽוֹנָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And say to [the] forest of the Negev, Hear [the] word of Yahweh; thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Behold, I [am] kindling in you a fire, and it will devour in you every tree green and every tree dry; not will be quenched [the] flame blazing, and will be scorched by it all faces from south to north.

en.L: And say to the forest of the Negev, Listen to the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: See, I am kindling a fire in you, and it will devour in you every green tree and every dry tree; the blazing flame will not be quenched, and all faces from south to north will be scorched by it.
en.B: Say to the forest of the Negev: Hear what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has to say. The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: I am about to kindle a fire in you, and it will consume every green tree and every dry tree in you. The blazing flame will not be put out, and every face from south to north will be scorched by it.
en.R: Tell the forest of the Negev, Listen to what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says. This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: I am going to start a fire in you. It will burn up every tree, both green and dry. The blazing flames will not be put out. Everyone from south to north will feel the heat of the fire on their faces.

fr.L: Et dis à la forêt du Néguev : Écoute la parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. Ainsi parle le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} : Voici, j’allume en toi un feu, et il dévorera en toi tout arbre vert et tout arbre sec ; la flamme ardente ne s’éteindra pas, et tous les visages du sud au nord en seront brûlés.
fr.B: Dis à la forêt du Néguev : Écoute la parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. Le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} dit ceci : Je vais allumer en toi un feu, et il dévorera chez toi tout arbre vert et tout arbre sec. La flamme ardente ne s’éteindra pas, et tous les visages, du sud au nord, en seront brûlés.
fr.R: Dis à la forêt du Néguev : Écoute ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Voici ce que dit le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} : Je vais mettre le feu chez toi. Il brûlera tous les arbres, les verts comme les secs. Personne ne pourra éteindre les flammes. Du sud au nord, tout le monde sentira la chaleur du feu sur son visage.

es.L: Y di al bosque del Néguev: Oye la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. Así dice el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}: Mira, yo enciendo en ti un fuego, y devorará en ti todo árbol verde y todo árbol seco; no se apagará la llama ardiente, y serán quemados por ella todos los rostros, desde el sur hasta el norte.
es.B: Di al bosque del Néguev: Escucha la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. El Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}} dice esto: Voy a encender en ti un fuego, y consumirá en ti todo árbol verde y todo árbol seco. La llama ardiente no se apagará, y todos los rostros, desde el sur hasta el norte, quedarán quemados por ella.
es.R: Dile al bosque del Néguev: Escucha este mensaje {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. Esto es lo que dice el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}: Voy a prender fuego en ti. Quemará todos los árboles, tanto los verdes como los secos. Las llamas ardientes no se apagarán. Todos, desde el sur hasta el norte, sentirán en la cara el calor del fuego.

decisions.choice: every green tree and every dry tree: all, without exception
decisions.reason: Green wood and dry wood together stand for everything in the forest. Verse 8 explains them as "the righteous and the wicked". Jesus uses a similar picture of green and dry wood in Luke 23:31.

decisions.choice: all faces from south to north: everyone in the land
decisions.reason: The fire is so great that every face will feel its heat. "From south to north" means the whole land, as in verse 9.

decisions.choice: I am about to kindle (B); I am going to start a fire (R)
decisions.reason: "See" with a participle marks something God is about to do. Literal keeps "See"; Balanced and Readable put it as an action about to happen, as in Jeremiah 21:4. Readable says what "scorched faces" means.

decisions.choice: Oye (L) / Escucha (B, R) la palabra del SEÑOR, in the singular
decisions.reason: The forest is addressed as one, so the verbs and 'ti' are singular; the call is worded as in Spanish Isaiah and Jeremiah.

source.text: וְרָאוּ֙ כָּל־בָּשָׂ֔ר כִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה בִּֽעַרְתִּ֑יהָ לֹ֖א תִּכְבֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And will see all flesh that I, Yahweh, kindled it; not will it be quenched.

en.L: And all flesh will see that I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, kindled it; it will not be quenched.
en.B: Everyone will see that I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have set it ablaze; it will not be put out.
en.R: Everyone will see that I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, started the fire. No one will be able to put it out.

fr.L: Et toute chair verra que moi, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, je l’ai allumé ; il ne s’éteindra pas.
fr.B: Tout le monde verra que c’est moi, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, qui l’ai allumé ; il ne s’éteindra pas.
fr.R: Tout le monde verra que c’est moi, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, qui ai allumé ce feu. Personne ne pourra l’éteindre.

es.B: Todos verán que yo, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, lo he encendido; no se apagará.
es.R: Todos verán que yo, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, prendí el fuego. Nadie podrá apagarlo.

decisions.choice: all flesh: all people
decisions.reason: "Flesh" stands for human beings in their weakness, and "all flesh" means everyone (Isaiah 40:5-6). The same words return in verses 9-10.

decisions.choice: everyone
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the idiom means (m1); Literal keeps it.

records.literal_gloss: And I said, Ah, Lord Yahweh! They [are] saying of me, Is he not a maker of parables?

en.L: Then I said, "Ah, Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}! They say of me, 'Is he not a speaker of parables?'"
en.B: Then I said, "Ah, Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}! They are saying about me, 'Is he not just telling parables?'"
en.R: Then I said, "Oh, Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}! People are saying about me, 'He is only telling riddles!'"

fr.L: Alors je dis : « Ah ! Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} ! Ils disent de moi : “N’est-ce pas un faiseur de paraboles ?” »
fr.B: Alors je dis : « Ah ! Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} ! Ils disent de moi : “Il ne fait que raconter des paraboles !” »
fr.R: Alors j’ai dit : « Oh non, Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} ! Les gens disent de moi : “Il ne fait que raconter des énigmes !” »

es.L: Entonces dije: «¡Ah, Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}! Ellos dicen de mí: “¿No es este un decidor de parábolas?”».
es.B: Entonces dije: «¡Ay, Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}! Andan diciendo de mí: “¿No está este contando parábolas?”».
es.R: Entonces dije: «¡Oh no, Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}! La gente dice de mí: “¡Solo está contando adivinanzas!”».

decisions.choice: a speaker of parables: someone who talks in figures and riddles
decisions.reason: The word for parable covers proverbs, riddles and figures of speech (17:2; 24:3). The people dismiss Ezekiel's word as clever pictures with no plain meaning, much as they later enjoy his preaching like a love song and do nothing about it (33:30-32).

decisions.choice: the prophet's complaint, and the LORD's answer in verses 6-12
decisions.reason: The LORD answers by saying the same thing again without the picture: the south is Jerusalem, the forest is the land of Israel, and the fire is the sword (verses 7-9).

decisions.choice: Ezekiel's words in double quotes, the people's words in single quotes
decisions.reason: Ezekiel's own words to God are part of his narrative and take quotation marks, as narrative speech does; the people's saying inside them takes single quotes. "Ah" follows the wording of a plea in Jeremiah ("Ah" / "Ah" / "Oh"). Readable gives the people's question as the scornful statement it is.

decisions.choice: ¡Ah, Señor DIOS! (L); ¡Ay, Señor DIOS! (B); ¡Oh no, Señor DIOS! (R); Ezekiel's words in « », the people's in “ ”
decisions.reason: The cry is worded as Spanish Jeremiah 1:6 at each level. Ezekiel's words are human speech, so they take « », with “ ” for the saying quoted inside.

decisions.choice: "Ah ! Seigneur DIEU !" (L, B); "Oh non, Seigneur DIEU !" (R), as Jeremiah 1:6; Ezekiel's words in « », the people's in “ ”; "je dis" (L, B), "j'ai dit" (R) in the narrative frame
decisions.reason: The settled French cry for *'ahah Adonai YHWH*; French puts a quotation inside a quotation in English-style double quotes.

decisions.choice: verse numbers: Hebrew 21:6-37 is 21:1-32 in many Bibles
decisions.reason: This translation numbers verses as the Hebrew text does. In many Bibles the five verses before this one are numbered 20:45-49, so this verse and the rest of the chapter (21:6-37 here) are numbered 21:1-32 there. The words are the same; only the numbers differ. Ezekiel is cited by the Hebrew numbers.

en.L: Son of man, set your face toward Jerusalem, and drip [words] against the sanctuaries, and prophesy against the land of Israel.
en.B: Son of man, turn to face Jerusalem. Preach against the holy places, and prophesy against the land of Israel.
en.R: Son of man, turn toward Jerusalem. Speak out against its holy places. Prophesy against the land of Israel.

fr.L: Fils d’homme, tourne ta face vers Jérusalem, et fais couler [tes paroles] vers les sanctuaires, et prophétise contre le pays d’Israël.
fr.B: Fils d’homme, tourne ton regard vers Jérusalem. Prêche contre les lieux saints, et prophétise contre le pays d’Israël.
fr.R: Fils d’homme, tourne-toi vers Jérusalem. Parle contre ses lieux saints. Prophétise contre le pays d’Israël.

es.L: Hijo de hombre, pon tu rostro hacia Jerusalén, y derrama [palabras] contra los santuarios, y profetiza contra la tierra de Israel.
es.B: Hijo de hombre, vuélvete de cara a Jerusalén. Predica contra los lugares santos y profetiza contra la tierra de Israel.
es.R: Hijo de hombre, vuélvete hacia Jerusalén. Habla en contra de sus lugares santos. Profetiza contra la tierra de Israel.

decisions.choice: the picture of verse 2 explained
decisions.reason: The three lines match the three lines of verse 2: the south is Jerusalem, the southland is the sanctuaries, and the forest of the Negev is the land of Israel. The fire of verse 3 will be the sword of verse 8.

decisions.choice: the sanctuaries: the temple and its holy places
alternatives: the many holy places of the land
decisions.reason: The word is plural. Beside Jerusalem it most likely means the temple and its courts, the holy places of the city (compare 7:24, where God says he will profane "their holy places").

source.text: וְאָמַרְתָּ֞ לְאַדְמַ֣ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הִנְנִ֣י אֵלַ֔יִךְ וְהוֹצֵאתִ֥י חַרְבִּ֖י מִתַּעְרָ֑הּ וְהִכְרַתִּ֥י מִמֵּ֖ךְ צַדִּ֥יק וְרָשָֽׁע׃

records.literal_gloss: And say to [the] land of Israel, Thus says Yahweh: Behold, I [am] against you, and I will draw my sword from its sheath, and I will cut off from you righteous and wicked.

en.L: And say to the land of Israel, Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: See, I [am] against you, and I will draw {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sword out of its sheath and cut off from you [both] righteous and wicked.
en.B: Say to the land of Israel, {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: I am against you. I will draw {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sword out of its sheath and cut off both righteous and wicked from among you.
en.R: Tell the land of Israel, This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: I am against you. I will pull {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sword out of its sheath. I will kill both those who do right and those who do wrong.

fr.L: Et dis au pays d’Israël : Ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : Voici, [je suis] contre toi, et je tirerai {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} épée de son fourreau, et je retrancherai de toi le juste et le méchant.
fr.B: Dis au pays d’Israël : {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit ceci : Je suis contre toi. Je tirerai {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} épée de son fourreau et je retrancherai du milieu de toi le juste comme le méchant.
fr.R: Dis au pays d’Israël : Voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : Je suis contre toi. Je vais sortir {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} épée de son fourreau. Je tuerai ceux qui font le bien comme ceux qui font le mal.

es.L: Y di a la tierra de Israel: Así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: Mira, yo [estoy] contra ti, y sacaré {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} espada de su vaina y cortaré de ti al justo y al malvado.
es.B: Di a la tierra de Israel: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dice esto: Estoy contra ti. Sacaré {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} espada de su vaina y eliminaré de en medio de ti tanto al justo como al malvado.
es.R: Dile a la tierra de Israel: Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: Estoy contra ti. Sacaré {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} espada de su vaina. Mataré tanto a los que hacen el bien como a los que hacen el mal.

decisions.choice: righteous and wicked: the coming disaster will sweep away everyone in the land
alternatives: the wicked only, as the Greek reads ("the unrighteous and the lawless")
decisions.reason: This is the plain meaning of the green and dry trees of verse 3. It sits uneasily beside chapters 9 and 18, where God spares those who mourn over the city's sins (9:4) and judges each person by their own deeds (18:20). The point here is the scale of the disaster: when the sword falls on a city, it does not choose. The Septuagint reads "the unrighteous and the lawless", softening the hard saying; the Hebrew is followed.

decisions.choice: Thus says the LORD: the divine name alone, not "the Lord GOD"
decisions.reason: Most of Ezekiel's messenger formulas have "the Lord GOD"; this one has the divine name alone, and the translation follows the text.

decisions.choice: those who do right and those who do wrong
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain words for the two kinds of people and says "kill" for "cut off", which here means to put to death by the sword.

decisions.choice: Así dice el SEÑOR (L); El SEÑOR dice esto (B); Esto es lo que dice el SEÑOR (R)
decisions.reason: Here the Hebrew has the divine name alone, so the formula is the one used for YHWH, without 'el Señor'. The land is addressed as one, with singular 'ti'.

decisions.choice: "Ainsi parle le SEIGNEUR :" / "Le SEIGNEUR dit ceci :" / "Voici ce que dit le SEIGNEUR :", with the divine name alone
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has YHWH without Adonai here, so French uses the shorter formula of Isaiah and Jeremiah.

source.text: יַ֛עַן אֲשֶׁר־הִכְרַ֥תִּי מִמֵּ֖ךְ צַדִּ֣יק וְרָשָׁ֑ע לָ֠כֵן תֵּצֵ֨א חַרְבִּ֧י מִתַּעְרָ֛הּ אֶל־כָּל־בָּשָׂ֖ר מִנֶּ֥גֶב צָפֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: Because that I will cut off from you righteous and wicked, therefore will go out my sword from its sheath against all flesh from south [to] north.

en.L: Because I will cut off from you [both] righteous and wicked, therefore {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sword will go out from its sheath against all flesh from south [to] north.
en.B: Because I will cut off from you both the righteous and the wicked, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sword will come out of its sheath against everyone from south to north.
en.R: I will kill both those who do right and those who do wrong. That is why I will pull {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sword out of its sheath and use it against everyone from south to north.

fr.L: Parce que je retrancherai de toi le juste et le méchant, à cause de cela {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} épée sortira de son fourreau contre toute chair, du sud au nord.
fr.B: Parce que je retrancherai du milieu de toi le juste comme le méchant, {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} épée sortira de son fourreau contre tout le monde, du sud au nord.
fr.R: Je tuerai ceux qui font le bien comme ceux qui font le mal. C’est pourquoi je vais sortir {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} épée de son fourreau et {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}en servir contre tout le monde, du sud au nord.

es.L: Por cuanto cortaré de ti al justo y al malvado, por tanto {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} espada saldrá de su vaina contra toda carne, desde el sur [hasta el] norte.
es.B: Porque eliminaré de en medio de ti tanto al justo como al malvado, {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} espada saldrá de su vaina contra todos, desde el sur hasta el norte.
es.R: Mataré tanto a los que hacen el bien como a los que hacen el mal. Por eso sacaré {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} espada de su vaina y la usaré contra todos, desde el sur hasta el norte.

decisions.choice: because ... therefore: the verse repeats verse 8 to drive it home
decisions.reason: The first half restates the last words of verse 8, and the second half draws the conclusion: the sword will reach "all flesh", the whole land, as the fire did in verse 3.

decisions.choice: everyone
decisions.reason: As in verse 4, Balanced and Readable say "everyone" for "all flesh".

source.text: וְיָֽדְעוּ֙ כָּל־בָּשָׂ֔ר כִּ֚י אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֔ה הוֹצֵ֥אתִי חַרְבִּ֖י מִתַּעְרָ֑הּ לֹ֥א תָשׁ֖וּב עֽוֹד׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And will know all flesh that I, Yahweh, have drawn out my sword from its sheath; not will it return again.

en.L: And all flesh will know that I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have drawn {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sword from its sheath; it will not go back again.
en.B: Then everyone will know that I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have drawn {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sword from its sheath; it will not go back again.
en.R: Then everyone will know that I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have pulled {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sword out of its sheath. I will not put it back.

fr.L: Et toute chair saura que moi, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, j’ai tiré {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} épée de son fourreau ; elle n’y retournera plus.
fr.B: Alors tout le monde saura que moi, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, j’ai tiré {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} épée de son fourreau ; elle n’y retournera plus.
fr.R: Alors tout le monde saura que moi, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, j’ai sorti {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} épée de son fourreau. Je ne l’y remettrai pas.

es.L: Y sabrá toda carne que yo, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, he sacado {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} espada de su vaina; no volverá más.
es.B: Entonces todos sabrán que yo, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, he sacado {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} espada de su vaina; no volverá a ella.
es.R: Entonces todos sabrán que yo, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, he sacado {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} espada de su vaina. No la volveré a guardar.

decisions.choice: all flesh will know that I, the LORD: the book's refrain, widened to all people
decisions.reason: The refrain "you will know that I am the LORD" (see 6:7) here takes the form "all flesh will know that I, the LORD, have ...": everyone will see who has done this.

decisions.choice: it will not return again: the sword will not be sheathed until its work is done
decisions.reason: Compare Isaiah 45:23 and 55:11, where God's word goes out and does not return without doing what he sent it to do.

source.text: וְאַתָּ֥ה בֶן־אָדָ֖ם הֵֽאָנַ֑ח בְּשִׁבְר֤וֹן מָתְנַ֨יִם֙ וּבִמְרִיר֔וּת תֵּֽאָנַ֖ח לְעֵינֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And you, son of man, groan; with breaking of loins and with bitterness groan before their eyes.

en.L: And you, son of man, groan! With breaking loins and with bitterness you shall groan before their eyes.
en.B: As for you, son of man, groan! Groan before their eyes with a body doubled over and with bitter grief.
en.R: Son of man, groan in front of them. Groan as if your body were breaking. Groan with bitter grief.

fr.L: Et toi, fils d’homme, gémis ! Les reins brisés et avec amertume, tu gémiras sous leurs yeux.
fr.B: Quant à toi, fils d’homme, gémis ! Gémis sous leurs yeux, plié en deux, dans un chagrin amer.
fr.R: Fils d’homme, gémis devant eux. Gémis comme si ton corps se brisait. Gémis dans un chagrin amer.

es.L: Y tú, hijo de hombre, ¡gime! Con quebranto de lomos y con amargura gemirás delante de sus ojos.
es.B: En cuanto a ti, hijo de hombre, ¡gime! Gime delante de ellos con el cuerpo doblado y con amargo dolor.
es.R: Hijo de hombre, gime delante de ellos. Gime como si se te estuviera rompiendo el cuerpo. Gime con amargo dolor.

decisions.choice: breaking loins: anguish that doubles the body over
decisions.reason: The loins, the hips and lower back, are where the body feels strength and pain. A grief that "breaks" them is anguish felt in the whole body, as in Isaiah 21:3 and Nahum 2:11.

decisions.choice: before their eyes: a sign acted out in front of the exiles
decisions.reason: Like Ezekiel's other sign-acts (4:1-5:4; 12:3-7), the groaning is done in public so that people will ask what it means (verse 12).

decisions.choice: with a body doubled over (B); as if your body were breaking (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable describe the body's anguish in plain words (m1).

source.text: וְהָיָה֙ כִּֽי־יֹאמְר֣וּ אֵלֶ֔יךָ עַל־מָ֖ה אַתָּ֣ה נֶאֱנָ֑ח וְאָמַרְתָּ֡ אֶל־שְׁמוּעָ֣ה כִֽי־בָאָ֡ה וְנָמֵ֣ס כָּל־לֵב֩ וְרָפ֨וּ כָל־יָדַ֜יִם וְכִהֲתָ֣ה כָל־ר֗וּחַ וְכָל־בִּרְכַּ֨יִם֙ תֵּלַ֣כְנָה מַּ֔יִם הִנֵּ֤ה בָאָה֙ וְנִֽהְיָ֔תָה נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And it will be when they say to you, On account of what [are] you groaning? and you shall say, Because of [the] news that [is] coming; and will melt every heart, and will go limp all hands, and will be faint every spirit, and all knees will go [to] water. Behold, it is coming, and it will happen, declares [the] Lord Yahweh.

en.L: And when they say to you, "Why are you groaning?" you shall say, "Because of the news, for it is coming. Every heart will melt, and all hands will go limp, and every spirit will grow faint, and all knees will run with water. See, it is coming, and it will happen, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}."
en.B: And when they ask you, "Why do you groan?" answer them, "Because of the news, for it is on its way. Every heart will melt, every hand will go limp, every spirit will grow faint, and every knee will be weak as water. It is coming! It will surely happen, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}."
en.R: When people ask you, "Why are you groaning?" tell them, "Because of the news that is coming. When it comes, everyone will lose courage. Their hands will hang limp. They will feel faint, and their knees will shake. It is coming! It will surely happen, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}."

fr.L: Et quand ils te diront : « Pourquoi gémis-tu ? » tu diras : « À cause de la nouvelle, car elle arrive. Tout cœur fondra, et toutes les mains faibliront, et tout esprit défaillira, et tous les genoux ruisselleront d’eau. Voici, elle arrive, et elle se réalisera, déclare le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}}. »
fr.B: Et quand ils te demanderont : « Pourquoi gémis-tu ? » réponds-leur : « À cause de la nouvelle, car elle est en route. Tous les cœurs fondront, toutes les mains faibliront, tous les esprits défailliront, et tous les genoux deviendront faibles comme de l’eau. Elle arrive ! Elle va se réaliser, déclare le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}}. »
fr.R: Quand les gens te demanderont : « Pourquoi gémis-tu ? » dis-leur : « À cause de la nouvelle qui arrive. Quand elle viendra, tout le monde perdra courage. Leurs mains tomberont sans force. Ils se sentiront défaillir, et leurs genoux trembleront. Elle arrive ! Elle va se réaliser, dit le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}}. »

es.L: Y cuando te digan: «¿Por qué gimes?», dirás: «Por la noticia, porque viene. Y todo corazón se derretirá, y todas las manos se debilitarán, y todo espíritu desfallecerá, y todas las rodillas se volverán agua. Mira, viene y sucederá, declara el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}».
es.B: Y cuando te pregunten: «¿Por qué gimes?», respóndeles: «Por la noticia, porque ya está en camino. Todo corazón se derretirá, toda mano quedará sin fuerza, todo espíritu desfallecerá y toda rodilla se volverá débil como el agua. ¡Ya viene! Sucederá sin falta, afirma el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}».
es.R: Cuando la gente te pregunte: «¿Por qué gimes?», diles: «Por la noticia que está por llegar. Cuando llegue, todos perderán el valor. Las manos les colgarán sin fuerza. Se sentirán desfallecer, y les temblarán las rodillas. ¡Ya viene! Sucederá sin falta, dice el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}».

decisions.choice: melting hearts, limp hands, faint spirits, knees turned to water: utter terror
alternatives: knees wet with urine from fear
decisions.reason: Each picture is a sign of terror: courage melts (Joshua 2:11), hands drop (Jeremiah 6:24), the spirit fails, and the knees give way. The last phrase, also in 7:17, may mean that the knees shake like water, or that people wet themselves for fear.

decisions.choice: the news that is coming: the report of Jerusalem's fall
decisions.reason: The news is not named. It is the disaster of the sword (verses 8-10), and in 24:26 and 33:21 a survivor brings Ezekiel the report that the city has fallen.

decisions.choice: everyone will lose courage ... their knees will shake
alternatives: every heart will melt ... all knees will run with water
decisions.reason: Readable says what the pictures mean (m1). Literal and Balanced keep them. The quotation marks follow the narrative frame: the people's question and Ezekiel's answer are speech within the LORD's instructions to him.

decisions.choice: todos perderán el valor ... les temblarán las rodillas
decisions.reason: R says what the four pictures of terror mean, as the English R does.

records.literal_gloss: And was [the] word of Yahweh to me, saying:

en.B: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} gave me this message:

fr.B: La parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} me fut adressée :
