es.B: La palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} vino a mí:
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me dio este mensaje:

decisions.choice: the formula as in Jeremiah
decisions.reason: The formula is worded as at verses 1 and 6. A new message begins: the song of the sword (verses 14-22).

source.text: בֶּן־אָדָ֕ם הִנָּבֵא֙ וְאָ֣מַרְתָּ֔ כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר אֲדֹנָ֑י אֱמֹ֕ר חֶ֥רֶב חֶ֛רֶב הוּחַ֖דָּה וְגַם־מְרוּטָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Son of man, prophesy and say, Thus says [the] Lord: Say, A sword, a sword, sharpened and also polished!

en.L: Son of man, prophesy and say, Thus says the Lord: \q Say: A sword, a sword is sharpened, and also polished!
en.B: Son of man, prophesy and say, The Lord says this: \q Say: A sword, a sword, sharpened and polished!
en.R: Son of man, prophesy. Tell them, This is what the Lord says: \q A sword, a sword is sharpened and polished!

fr.L: Fils d’homme, prophétise et dis : Ainsi parle le Seigneur : \q Dis : Une épée, une épée est aiguisée, et aussi polie !
fr.B: Fils d’homme, prophétise et dis : Le Seigneur dit ceci : \q Dis : L’épée, l’épée, aiguisée et polie !
fr.R: Fils d’homme, prophétise. Dis-leur : Voici ce que dit le Seigneur : \q Une épée, une épée est aiguisée et polie !

es.L: Hijo de hombre, profetiza y di: Así dice el Señor: \q Di: ¡Una espada, una espada está afilada, y también pulida!
es.B: Hijo de hombre, profetiza y di: El Señor dice esto: \q Di: ¡Una espada, una espada, afilada y pulida!
es.R: Hijo de hombre, profetiza. Diles: Esto es lo que dice el Señor: \q ¡Una espada, una espada está afilada y pulida!

decisions.choice: the song of the sword (verses 14-22): a poem in short, fierce lines
decisions.reason: Verses 14-22 are poetry: short lines, repeated words ("a sword, a sword"; "sharpened", "polished") and cries. Many think it was a war song or a sword dance that Ezekiel took up, with the clapping of hands in verses 19 and 22. Several lines (verses 15, 18, 19, 20) are among the hardest in the book, and the notes say so where they come.

decisions.choice: Thus says the Lord: "Lord" alone, without the divine name
decisions.reason: Here the formula has only "the Lord" (Adonai), not the usual "the Lord GOD". The text is followed as it stands.

decisions.choice: sharpened and polished: made ready for battle
decisions.reason: A sword was sharpened to cut and polished, or burnished, so that it flashed (verse 15).

decisions.choice: Tell them
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "say" twice. Readable keeps one, since the second only repeats the first. The song (verses 14-22) is set in lines at every level, following the Hebrew accents.

decisions.choice: Así dice el Señor, with no divine_name span, and the song in lines
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has 'Lord' (Adonai) alone, so 'el Señor' stands without the span. The song of the sword (14-22) is set in lines, as in the English.

decisions.choice: the song of the sword (14-22) set in short lines (\q) at every level, in the present and future of speech; "le Seigneur" without the divine-name span
decisions.reason: Follows the English lines and the Hebrew division; the Hebrew has *Adonai* alone here, so French has no SEIGNEUR span.

decisions.choice: "prophétise et dis" at every level (R "prophétise. Dis-leur")
decisions.reason: The settled French wording for Ezekiel's commission.

source.text: לְמַ֨עַן טְבֹ֤חַ טֶ֨בַח֙ הוּחַ֔דָּה לְמַעַן־הֱיֵה־לָ֥הּ בָּ֖רָק מֹרָ֑טָּה א֣וֹ נָשִׂ֔ישׂ שֵׁ֥בֶט בְּנִ֖י מֹאֶ֥סֶת כָּל־עֵֽץ׃

records.literal_gloss: In order to slaughter a slaughter it is sharpened; in order that to it [be] lightning, it is polished. Or shall we rejoice? [The] rod of my son despises every tree.

en.L: In order to slaughter a slaughter it is sharpened, \q in order that it may have lightning it is polished. \q Or shall we rejoice? \q The rod of my son despises every tree.
en.B: It is sharpened for slaughter, \q polished to flash like lightning. \q Or should we rejoice? \q The rod of my son despises every tree.
en.R: It is sharpened for killing, \q polished to flash like lightning. \q Should we be glad? \q The rod of my son looks down on every tree.

fr.L: C’est pour massacrer un massacre qu’elle est aiguisée, \q c’est pour qu’elle ait l’éclair qu’elle est polie. \q Ou bien nous réjouirons-nous ? \q Le sceptre de mon fils méprise tout arbre.
fr.B: Elle est aiguisée pour le massacre, \q polie pour briller comme l’éclair. \q Ou bien devrions-nous nous réjouir ? \q Le sceptre de mon fils méprise tout arbre.
fr.R: Elle est aiguisée pour tuer, \q polie pour briller comme l’éclair. \q Devrions-nous être contents ? \q Le sceptre de mon fils regarde de haut tous les arbres.

es.L: Para degollar una matanza está afilada, \q para que tenga relámpago está pulida. \q ¿O nos alegraremos? \q La vara de mi hijo desprecia todo árbol.
es.B: Está afilada para la matanza, \q pulida para brillar como relámpago. \q ¿O deberíamos alegrarnos? \q La vara de mi hijo desprecia todo árbol.
es.R: Está afilada para matar, \q pulida para brillar como relámpago. \q ¿Deberíamos estar contentos? \q La vara de mi hijo menosprecia todo árbol.

decisions.choice: Or shall we rejoice? The rod of my son despises every tree: the Hebrew words are kept as they stand; their sense is uncertain
alternatives: the sword despises the royal scepter of Judah ("my son") as if it were mere wood (compare Genesis 49:10)
the sword is the rod with which God punishes his son Israel, and it scorns every lesser rod of punishment
a corrupted text, which some correct to "you have despised the rod and every warning"
decisions.reason: The words read "or shall we rejoice? the rod of my son despises every tree". The "rod" (also "scepter", "tribe") may be the scepter promised to Judah in Genesis 49:10, and "my son" may be Israel (Exodus 4:22) or Judah's king (2 Samuel 7:14). The same "rod" that "despises" returns in verse 18. No reading is certain, and none is chosen here.

decisions.choice: that it may have lightning: so that it flashes like lightning
decisions.reason: A polished blade gleams. Deuteronomy 32:41 speaks of God's "flashing sword", and Nahum 3:3 and Habakkuk 3:11 of the lightning of spears and swords.

decisions.choice: The rod of my son despises every tree, at every level
alternatives: a smoothed rendering choosing one reading
decisions.reason: Because the sense is uncertain (m1), every level keeps the Hebrew's words; Readable uses only plainer words.

decisions.choice: La vara de mi hijo desprecia (L, B) / menosprecia (R) todo árbol, kept word for word
decisions.reason: The sense of these words is uncertain, so every level keeps them as they stand, as the English does, and the footnote gives the question.

decisions.choice: "le sceptre de mon fils" at every level, no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The obscure Hebrew is kept as it stands, as in the English; *shevet* is "sceptre" in the royal sense of verse 18 and 19:11. The English has no span on "my son".

source.text: וַיִּתֵּ֥ן אֹתָ֛הּ לְמָרְטָ֖ה לִתְפֹּ֣שׂ בַּכָּ֑ף הִֽיא־הוּחַ֤דָּה חֶ֨רֶב֙ וְהִ֣יא מֹרָ֔טָּה לָתֵ֥ת אוֹתָ֖הּ בְּיַד־הוֹרֵֽג׃

records.literal_gloss: And one gave it to be polished, to be grasped in the hand; it is sharpened, a sword, and it is polished, to give it into [the] hand of a killer.

en.L: And it is handed over to be polished, so that it may be grasped in the hand; \q it is sharpened, the sword, and it is polished, \q to put it into the hand of the slayer.
en.B: The sword is handed over for polishing, ready for the hand to grasp; \q it is sharpened and polished, \q to be put into the hand of the killer.
en.R: The sword is given to be polished, so that someone can hold it. \q It is sharp and shining, \q ready for a killer to use.

fr.L: Et on l’a donnée à polir, pour qu’on la saisisse en main ; \q elle est aiguisée, l’épée, et elle est polie, \q pour la mettre dans la main de celui qui tue.
fr.B: On a donné l’épée à polir, pour que la main la saisisse ; \q elle est aiguisée et polie, \q pour être mise dans la main du tueur.
fr.R: On a donné l’épée à polir, pour que quelqu’un puisse la tenir. \q Elle est tranchante et brillante, \q prête à servir à un tueur.

es.L: Y se la dio a pulir, para que sea empuñada con la mano; \q está afilada la espada, y está pulida, \q para ponerla en la mano del verdugo.
es.B: La espada se entrega para que la pulan, lista para que la mano la empuñe; \q está afilada y pulida \q para ponerla en la mano del que mata.
es.R: La espada se entrega para que la pulan, para que alguien pueda empuñarla. \q Está afilada y brillante, \q lista para que un asesino la use.

decisions.choice: it is given: the sword is handed over, without saying by whom
decisions.reason: The verb is active, "he gave", with no subject named; it works like a passive. Verse 8 has already said whose sword it is: the LORD's.

decisions.choice: the slayer: the one who will use the sword
decisions.reason: The "killer" is left unnamed in the song. Verse 24 makes plain that it is the king of Babylon.

source.text: זְעַ֤ק וְהֵילֵל֙ בֶּן־אָדָ֔ם כִּי־הִיא֙ הָיתָ֣הבְעַמִּ֔י הִ֖יא בְּכָל־נְשִׂיאֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל מְגוּרֵ֤י אֶל־חֶ֨רֶב֙ הָי֣וּ אֶת־עַמִּ֔י לָכֵ֖ן סְפֹ֥ק אֶל־יָרֵֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: Cry out and wail, son of man, for it is against my people, it [is] against all [the] princes of Israel; thrown to [the] sword they are with my people; therefore strike [your] thigh.

en.L: Cry out and wail, son of man, \q for it is against {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, \q it [is] against all the princes of Israel; \q thrown to the sword they are, with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people; \q therefore strike [your] thigh.
en.B: Cry out and wail, son of man, \q for it is against {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, \q against all the princes of Israel. \q They are thrown to the sword along with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people. \q So strike your thigh in grief.
en.R: Cry out and weep, son of man, \q because the sword is against {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people \q and against all the rulers of Israel. \q They and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people will be killed by the sword. \q So slap your thigh in grief.

fr.L: Crie et hurle, fils d’homme, \q car elle est contre {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple, \q elle [est] contre tous les princes d’Israël ; \q livrés à l’épée ils sont, avec {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple ; \q c’est pourquoi frappe[-toi] la cuisse.
fr.B: Crie et hurle, fils d’homme, \q car elle est contre {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple, \q contre tous les princes d’Israël. \q Ils sont livrés à l’épée avec {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple. \q Alors frappe-toi la cuisse de douleur.
fr.R: Crie et pleure, fils d’homme, \q car l’épée est contre {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple \q et contre tous les chefs d’Israël. \q Eux et {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple seront tués par l’épée. \q Alors frappe-toi la cuisse de douleur.

es.L: Clama y gime, hijo de hombre, \q porque ella está contra {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo, \q [está] contra todos los príncipes de Israel; \q arrojados a la espada están junto con {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo; \q por tanto, golpéate el muslo.
es.B: Clama y gime, hijo de hombre, \q porque ella está contra {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo, \q contra todos los príncipes de Israel. \q Son arrojados a la espada junto con {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo. \q Por eso golpéate el muslo de dolor.
es.R: Grita y llora, hijo de hombre, \q porque la espada está contra {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo \q y contra todos los gobernantes de Israel. \q Ellos y {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo morirán a espada. \q Por eso golpéate el muslo de dolor.

decisions.choice: strike your thigh: a gesture of grief and shock
decisions.reason: Striking the thigh shows dismay and sorrow (Jeremiah 31:19).

decisions.choice: the princes of Israel: the leaders, the king and the royal house
decisions.reason: Ezekiel uses this word for Israel's rulers, including King Zedekiah, whom he calls "the prince" (12:10; 21:30).

decisions.choice: rulers
decisions.reason: The word for prince is "prince" at Literal and Balanced and "ruler" at Readable, as set for Ezekiel. Balanced adds "in grief" to say what the gesture means (m1).

decisions.choice: golpéate el muslo (L); golpéate el muslo de dolor (B, R)
decisions.reason: The gesture of grief is worded as in Spanish Jeremiah 31:19.

source.text: כִּ֣י בֹ֔חַן וּמָ֕ה אִם־גַּם־שֵׁ֥בֶט מֹאֶ֖סֶת לֹ֣א יִֽהְיֶ֑ה נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: For [it is] a testing; and what if even [the] rod despising will not be? declares [the] Lord Yahweh.

en.L: For [it is] a testing; and what if even the rod that despises will not be? \q declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: For it is a time of testing. And what if even the rod that despises is no more? \q declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: A time of testing has come. What if even the rod that looks down on others is gone? \q says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

fr.L: Car [c’est] une épreuve ; et quoi, si même le sceptre qui méprise ne doit plus être ? \q déclare le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Car c’est un temps d’épreuve. Et si même le sceptre qui méprise n’existait plus ? \q déclare le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Le temps de l’épreuve est arrivé. Et si même le sceptre qui regarde les autres de haut disparaissait ? \q dit le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}}.

es.L: Porque [es] una prueba; ¿y qué si aun la vara que desprecia no existe más? \q declara el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}.
es.B: Porque es un tiempo de prueba. ¿Y qué, si aun la vara que desprecia deja de existir? \q afirma el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}.
es.R: Ha llegado un tiempo de prueba. ¿Y qué, si aun la vara que menosprecia a los demás desaparece? \q dice el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}.

decisions.choice: a testing has come; the despising rod may cease: the Hebrew words kept; the sense is uncertain
alternatives: "the test has come, and what if Judah's scepter, which scorned the warning, is no more?" (taking the rod as the royal line)
a damaged text that cannot be translated with confidence
decisions.reason: This verse is broken and very short in the Hebrew, and it picks up the "rod" that "despises" from verse 15. The most likely sense is that God is putting the people to the test, and that even the royal scepter of Judah may come to an end, as verse 32 will say. No reading is certain.

source.text: וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן־אָדָ֔ם הִנָּבֵ֕א וְהַ֖ךְ כַּ֣ף אֶל־כָּ֑ף וְתִכָּפֵ֞ל חֶ֤רֶב שְׁלִישִׁ֨תָה֙ חֶ֣רֶב חֲלָלִ֔ים הִ֗יא חֶ֚רֶב חָלָ֣ל הַגָּד֔וֹל הַחֹדֶ֖רֶת לָהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And you, son of man, prophesy and strike hand to hand, and let be doubled [the] sword, a third [time], [the] sword of slain ones; it [is the] sword of [the] slain, the great one, which surrounds them.

en.L: And you, son of man, prophesy \q and strike hand to hand; \q and let the sword be doubled, a third time, the sword of slain ones; \q it [is] the sword of the great slain one, which surrounds them.
en.B: So you, son of man, prophesy \q and clap your hands. \q Let the sword strike twice, even three times, the sword for the slain; \q it is the sword for the great slaughter, which closes in on them.
en.R: Son of man, prophesy \q and clap your hands. \q Let the sword strike again and again, the sword that kills; \q it is the sword for a great slaughter, closing in on them from all sides.

fr.L: Et toi, fils d’homme, prophétise \q et frappe main contre main ; \q et que l’épée soit redoublée, une troisième [fois], l’épée des tués ; \q c’[est] l’épée du grand tué, qui les encercle.
fr.B: Toi donc, fils d’homme, prophétise \q et bats des mains. \q Que l’épée frappe deux fois, et même trois, l’épée qui fait des victimes ; \q c’est l’épée du grand massacre, qui se referme sur eux.
fr.R: Fils d’homme, prophétise \q et bats des mains. \q Que l’épée frappe encore et encore, l’épée qui tue ; \q c’est l’épée d’un grand massacre, qui les entoure de tous côtés.

es.L: Y tú, hijo de hombre, profetiza \q y bate una mano contra otra; \q y que se duplique la espada, [y] por tercera vez, la espada de los muertos; \q es la espada del gran muerto, que los rodea.
es.B: Así que tú, hijo de hombre, profetiza \q y bate palmas. \q Que la espada golpee dos y hasta tres veces, la espada para los que mueren; \q es la espada de la gran matanza, que los va cercando.
es.R: Hijo de hombre, profetiza \q y bate palmas. \q Que la espada golpee una y otra vez, la espada que mata; \q es la espada para una gran matanza, que los cerca por todos lados.

decisions.choice: strike hand to hand: clapping, to rouse the sword
decisions.reason: Clapping can show scorn (25:6) or call others to action. Here the prophet claps to set the sword going, and in verse 22 the LORD does the same. In 6:11 Ezekiel is told to clap his hands and stamp his foot.

decisions.choice: let the sword be doubled, a third time: let it strike again and again
decisions.reason: The numbers stress how often the sword will strike: twice, three times, as many as it takes.

decisions.choice: the great slain one, which surrounds them: uncertain words
alternatives: "the great slaughter" (taking the word for "slain" as a collective)
"which enters their rooms" (from the word for an inner room)
decisions.reason: The phrase may mean "the sword for the great slaughter" or "the sword of the great one who is slain", perhaps the king. The last verb is found only here; it may mean "surround" or "penetrate", as into the inner rooms of a house.

decisions.choice: the great slaughter
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable take the phrase as "the great slaughter", the most likely sense (m3). Literal keeps the Hebrew's form.

source.text: לְמַ֣עַן׀לָמ֣וּג לֵ֗ב וְהַרְבֵּה֙ הַמִּכְשֹׁלִ֔ים עַ֚ל כָּל־שַׁ֣עֲרֵיהֶ֔ם נָתַ֖תִּי אִבְחַת־חָ֑רֶב אָ֛ח עֲשׂוּיָ֥ה לְבָרָ֖ק מְעֻטָּ֥ה לְטָֽבַח׃

records.literal_gloss: So that to melt [the] heart and many the stumbling, at all their gates I have set [the] point of [the] sword. Ah! It is made for lightning, grasped for slaughter.

en.L: so that the heart may melt and the stumblings be many, \q at all their gates I have set the point of the sword. \q Ah! It is made for lightning, it is grasped for slaughter.
en.B: so that hearts may melt and many may fall. \q At all their gates I have set the point of the sword. \q Ah! It is made to flash like lightning, drawn for slaughter.
en.R: This will make people lose courage, and many will fall. \q I have placed the sword at all their city gates. \q It flashes like lightning, ready to kill.

fr.L: afin que le cœur fonde et que les chutes se multiplient, \q à toutes leurs portes j’ai placé la pointe de l’épée. \q Ah ! Elle est faite pour l’éclair, elle est saisie pour le massacre.
fr.B: afin que les cœurs fondent et que beaucoup tombent. \q À toutes leurs portes j’ai placé la pointe de l’épée. \q Ah ! Elle est faite pour briller comme l’éclair, tirée pour le massacre.
fr.R: Les gens perdront courage, et beaucoup tomberont. \q J’ai placé l’épée à toutes les portes de leurs villes. \q Elle brille comme l’éclair, prête à tuer.

es.L: para que se derrita el corazón y se multipliquen los tropiezos, \q en todas sus puertas he puesto la punta de la espada. \q ¡Ah! Está hecha para relámpago, empuñada para la matanza.
es.B: para que se derritan los corazones y caigan muchos. \q En todas sus puertas he puesto la punta de la espada. \q ¡Ah! Está hecha para brillar como relámpago, desenvainada para la matanza.
es.R: Esto hará que la gente pierda el valor y que muchos caigan. \q He puesto la espada en todas las puertas de sus ciudades. \q Brilla como relámpago, lista para matar.

decisions.choice: the point of the sword: an uncertain word
decisions.reason: The word translated "point" is found only here, and its meaning is guessed from the context. Old translations give "slaughter" or "terror".

decisions.choice: grasped: an uncertain word, perhaps "drawn" or "wrapped"
decisions.reason: This word is also rare. It may mean drawn or grasped, or wrapped with a grip. The sense is plain: the sword is ready for slaughter.

decisions.choice: at all their gates: where the people gathered and the city was defended
decisions.reason: The city gates were the place of business and the point an enemy attacked. The sword stands where the people come and go.

decisions.choice: make people lose courage, and many will fall
alternatives: so that the heart may melt and the stumblings be many
decisions.reason: Readable says what melting hearts mean (verse 12) and starts a new sentence, since the verse continues the thought of verse 19.

source.text: הִתְאַחֲדִ֥י הֵימִ֖נִי הָשִׂ֣ימִי הַשְׂמִ֑ילִי אָ֖נָה פָּנַ֥יִךְ מֻעָדֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: Slash! To the right! Set yourself! To the left! Wherever your edge is appointed.

en.L: Slash to the right! Set [yourself], to the left! \q wherever your edge is appointed.
en.B: Slash to the right; turn to the left, \q wherever your edge is aimed!
en.R: Sword, cut to the right and to the left, \q wherever your blade is pointed!

fr.L: Frappe à droite ! Mets-[toi] à gauche ! \q là où ton tranchant est dirigé.
fr.B: Frappe à droite, tourne-toi à gauche, \q partout où ton tranchant est dirigé !
fr.R: Épée, frappe à droite et à gauche, \q partout où ta lame est tournée !

es.L: ¡Corta a la derecha! ¡Ponte a la izquierda! \q adonde tu filo esté destinado.
es.B: Corta a la derecha, vuélvete a la izquierda, \q ¡adonde apunte tu filo!
es.R: Espada, corta a la derecha y a la izquierda, \q ¡adonde apunte tu hoja!

decisions.choice: the sword is addressed, and told to cut in every direction
decisions.reason: The commands are spoken to the sword itself; "your edge" is literally "your face", the sword's blade. It is to strike on every side.

decisions.choice: Sword
decisions.reason: Readable names the sword, so that the reader knows who is addressed (m1).

source.text: וְגַם־אֲנִ֗י אַכֶּ֤ה כַפִּי֙ אֶל־כַּפִּ֔י וַהֲנִחֹתִ֖י חֲמָתִ֑י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבַּֽרְתִּי׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And also I will strike my hand to my hand, and I will cause my wrath to rest; I, Yahweh, have spoken.

en.L: And I also will strike {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand, and I will bring {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath to rest; \q I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have spoken.
en.B: I too will clap {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hands, and I will satisfy {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath. \q I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have spoken.
en.R: I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} will clap {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hands, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger will be satisfied. \q I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have spoken.

fr.L: Et moi aussi, je frapperai {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} main contre {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} main, et je ferai reposer {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} fureur ; \q moi, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, j’ai parlé.
fr.B: Moi aussi, je battrai des mains, et j’assouvirai {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} fureur. \q Moi, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, j’ai parlé.
fr.R: Moi aussi, je battrai des mains, et {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} colère sera apaisée. \q C’est moi, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, qui le dis.

es.L: Y también yo batiré {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} mano contra {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} mano, y haré reposar {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} furor; \q yo, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, he hablado.
es.B: También yo batiré palmas y saciaré {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} furor. \q Yo, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, he hablado.
es.R: Yo mismo batiré palmas, y {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} enojo quedará saciado. \q Yo, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, lo he dicho.

decisions.choice: I will bring my wrath to rest: I will let my anger run until it is spent
decisions.reason: The same words are used in 5:13, 16:42 and 24:13: God's anger will be satisfied by the punishment.

decisions.choice: I also will clap: God joins the prophet's gesture of verse 19
decisions.reason: The song ends with God himself doing what he told the prophet to do. "I, the LORD, have spoken" seals it, as in 5:13, 15 and 17.

decisions.choice: Yo, el SEÑOR, he hablado (L, B); Yo, el SEÑOR, lo he dicho (R)
decisions.reason: The closing seal keeps one wording at each level through the book.

decisions.choice: "Moi, le SEIGNEUR, j'ai parlé" (L, B); "C'est moi, le SEIGNEUR, qui le dis" (R), for the whole book
decisions.reason: The settled French wording of Ezekiel's closing seal.

source.text: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And was [the] word of Yahweh to me, saying:

en.L: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:
en.B: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} gave me this message:

fr.L: Et la parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} me fut adressée, disant :
fr.B: La parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} me fut adressée :
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} m’a donné ce message :

es.L: Vino a mí la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, diciendo:
es.B: La palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} vino a mí:
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me dio este mensaje:

decisions.choice: the formula as in Jeremiah
decisions.reason: A new message begins: the king of Babylon at the crossroads (verses 24-32). The chapter returns to prose.

source.text: וְאַתָּ֨ה בֶן־אָדָ֜ם שִׂים־לְךָ֣׀שְׁנַ֣יִם דְּרָכִ֗ים לָבוֹא֙ חֶ֣רֶב מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֔ל מֵאֶ֥רֶץ אֶחָ֖ד יֵצְא֣וּ שְׁנֵיהֶ֑ם וְיָ֣ד בָּרֵ֔א בְּרֹ֥אשׁ דֶּֽרֶךְ־עִ֖יר בָּרֵֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: And you, son of man, set for yourself two ways for the coming of [the] sword of [the] king of Babylon; from one land shall go out the two of them; and a hand cut out, at [the] head of [the] way of a city cut [it] out.

en.L: And you, son of man, mark out for yourself two ways for the sword of the king of Babylon to come; from one land the two of them shall go out. And carve a hand; at the head of the way to a city carve [it].
en.B: As for you, son of man, mark out two roads that the sword of the king of Babylon may take, both of them starting from one country. Carve a signpost, and set it where the road to a city begins.
en.R: Son of man, draw two roads that the king of Babylon and his army can take with their swords. Both roads start in the same country. Where the road divides, put up a sign that points the way to a city.

fr.L: Et toi, fils d’homme, trace-toi deux chemins pour la venue de l’épée du roi de Babylone ; d’un seul pays ils sortiront tous les deux. Et grave une main ; à l’entrée du chemin d’une ville, grave[-la].
fr.B: Quant à toi, fils d’homme, trace deux routes que pourra prendre l’épée du roi de Babylone ; toutes deux partiront du même pays. Grave un poteau indicateur, et place-le là où commence la route d’une ville.
fr.R: Fils d’homme, dessine deux routes que le roi de Babylone et son armée pourront prendre avec leurs épées. Les deux routes partent du même pays. À l’endroit où la route se sépare, mets un panneau qui indique le chemin d’une ville.

es.L: Y tú, hijo de hombre, trázate dos caminos para que venga por ellos la espada del rey de Babilonia; de una misma tierra saldrán los dos. Y graba una mano; en el comienzo del camino a una ciudad grába[la].
es.B: En cuanto a ti, hijo de hombre, traza dos caminos que pueda tomar la espada del rey de Babilonia, los dos saliendo de un mismo país. Graba una señal, y ponla donde empieza el camino a una ciudad.
es.R: Hijo de hombre, dibuja dos caminos que el rey de Babilonia y su ejército puedan tomar con sus espadas. Los dos caminos salen del mismo país. Donde el camino se divide, pon una señal que indique el camino hacia una ciudad.

decisions.choice: mark out two roads: a sign-act, perhaps drawn on the ground or on a brick
decisions.reason: As in 4:1, where Ezekiel draws Jerusalem on a brick, he makes a map of the choice the king of Babylon will face.

decisions.choice: a hand: a signpost or marker
decisions.reason: "Hand" is used for a monument or marker (1 Samuel 15:12; 2 Samuel 18:18). Here it is a sign at the fork in the road, perhaps shaped like a hand pointing the way.

decisions.choice: the king of Babylon: Nebuchadnezzar, on his campaign against Judah and Ammon
decisions.reason: In 589-588 BC King Zedekiah rebelled against Babylon (2 Kings 24:20), and Ammon seems to have been among the neighbors who plotted with him (Jeremiah 27:3). Nebuchadnezzar marched west to put down the revolt, and Jerusalem was besieged from early 588 BC (2 Kings 25:1).

decisions.choice: a signpost (B); a sign that points the way (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the "hand" is (m2). Readable makes plain that the king's sword means his army.

decisions.choice: una señal (B); una señal que indique el camino (R); L keeps 'una mano'
decisions.reason: The Hebrew 'hand' here is a signpost; B and R give that sense in a plain word.

source.text: דֶּ֣רֶךְ תָּשִׂ֔ים לָב֣וֹא חֶ֔רֶב אֵ֖ת רַבַּ֣ת בְּנֵֽי־עַמּ֑וֹן וְאֶת־יְהוּדָ֥ה בִירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם בְּצוּרָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: A way you shall set for the coming of [the] sword to Rabbah of [the] sons of Ammon, and to Judah, into Jerusalem the fortified.

en.L: A way you shall mark out by which the sword may come to Rabbah of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Ammon, and [another] to Judah, into Jerusalem the fortified.
en.B: Mark one road for the sword to come to Rabbah of the Ammonites, and another to Judah and to Jerusalem, the fortified city.
en.R: Mark one road that leads the army to Rabbah, the Ammonite capital. Mark the other road to Judah and to Jerusalem, the city with strong walls.

fr.L: Tu traceras un chemin pour que l’épée vienne à Rabba des {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Ammon, et [un autre] vers Juda, dans Jérusalem la fortifiée.
fr.B: Trace une route pour que l’épée aille à Rabba des Ammonites, et une autre vers Juda et vers Jérusalem, la ville fortifiée.
fr.R: Trace une route qui mène l’armée à Rabba, la capitale des Ammonites. Trace l’autre route vers Juda et vers Jérusalem, la ville aux murailles solides.

es.L: Un camino trazarás para que venga la espada a Rabá de los hijos de Amón, y [otro] a Judá, a Jerusalén la fortificada.
es.B: Traza un camino para que la espada llegue a Rabá de los amonitas, y otro a Judá y a Jerusalén, la ciudad fortificada.
es.R: Traza un camino que lleve al ejército a Rabá, la capital de los amonitas. Traza el otro camino hacia Judá y Jerusalén, la ciudad de murallas fuertes.

decisions.choice: Rabbah of the Ammonites: the Ammonite capital, east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Rabbah lay on the site of modern Amman. Ammon also faced Babylon's anger, and 25:1-7 and 21:33-37 turn to it.

decisions.choice: Jerusalem the fortified: a city that trusted in its walls
decisions.reason: The word stresses the city's strength. It was strong enough to hold out for a year and a half, but not to be saved (2 Kings 25:1-4).

decisions.choice: the children of Ammon (L); the Ammonites (B, R)
decisions.reason: The wording follows Jeremiah 49:2, as published.

decisions.choice: los hijos de Amón (L); los amonitas (B, R), with no gender span
decisions.reason: 'Los hijos de Amón' is the published Spanish name of the people (Deuteronomy 3:11 L) and already includes women.

decisions.choice: "Rabba des {{gender:enfants|fils}} d'Ammon" (L); "Rabba des Ammonites" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The French forms of 1 Chronicles 20:1; the gender setting as the English Literal "children of Ammon".

source.text: כִּֽי־עָמַ֨ד מֶלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֜ל אֶל־אֵ֣ם הַדֶּ֗רֶךְ בְּרֹ֛אשׁ שְׁנֵ֥י הַדְּרָכִ֖ים לִקְסָם־קָ֑סֶם קִלְקַ֤ל בַּֽחִצִּים֙ שָׁאַ֣ל בַּתְּרָפִ֔ים רָאָ֖ה בַּכָּבֵֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: For stands [the] king of Babylon at [the] mother of the way, at [the] head of the two ways, to divine divination; he shakes the arrows, he asks the teraphim, he looks at the liver.

en.L: For the king of Babylon stands at the mother of the way, at the head of the two ways, to practice divination; he shakes the arrows, he consults the teraphim, he looks at the liver.
en.B: For the king of Babylon has stopped at the fork in the road, where the two roads begin, to look for an omen. He shakes the arrows, consults his household gods and examines the liver.
en.R: The king of Babylon will stop at the place where the road divides into two. He will look for a sign to show him which way to go. He will shake arrows marked with names. He will ask his household idols for advice. He will look closely at the liver of an animal he has sacrificed.

fr.L: Car le roi de Babylone se tient à la mère du chemin, à la tête des deux chemins, pour pratiquer la divination ; il secoue les flèches, il consulte les téraphim, il regarde le foie.
fr.B: Car le roi de Babylone s’est arrêté à la bifurcation, là où commencent les deux routes, pour chercher un présage. Il secoue les flèches, consulte ses dieux domestiques et examine le foie.
fr.R: Le roi de Babylone s’arrêtera à l’endroit où la route se sépare en deux. Il cherchera un signe qui lui montre quel chemin prendre. Il secouera des flèches marquées de noms. Il demandera conseil à ses idoles domestiques. Il examinera de près le foie d’un animal qu’il aura sacrifié.

es.L: Porque el rey de Babilonia se detiene en la madre del camino, en el comienzo de los dos caminos, para practicar adivinación; agita las flechas, consulta a los dioses domésticos, mira el hígado.
es.B: Porque el rey de Babilonia se ha detenido en la bifurcación, donde empiezan los dos caminos, para buscar un presagio. Agita las flechas, consulta a sus dioses domésticos y examina el hígado.
es.R: El rey de Babilonia se detendrá en el lugar donde el camino se divide en dos. Buscará una señal que le muestre por dónde ir. Agitará flechas marcadas con nombres. Pedirá consejo a sus ídolos de la familia. Examinará con cuidado el hígado de un animal sacrificado.

decisions.choice: the mother of the way: the fork in the road
decisions.reason: The road is pictured as a mother from which the two roads come.

decisions.choice: three ways of seeking an omen: drawing marked arrows, consulting the teraphim, reading the liver
decisions.reason: Arrows with names on them were shaken in a quiver, and the one drawn out gave the answer (verse 27). The teraphim were household gods or images that were consulted (Zechariah 10:2). Reading the liver of a sacrificed animal was a well-known art in Babylon, where clay models of livers marked for omens have been found.

decisions.choice: arrows marked with names; the liver of an animal he has sacrificed
decisions.reason: Readable explains each kind of omen (m2). "Teraphim" is "household gods" at Balanced and "household idols" at Readable, as in Hosea 3:4 and Zechariah 10:2.

decisions.choice: los dioses domésticos (L, B); sus ídolos de la familia (R)
decisions.reason: The teraphim are worded as in Spanish Genesis 31:19 and Judges 17:5.

decisions.choice: "les téraphim" (L); "ses dieux domestiques" (B), "ses idoles domestiques" (R)
decisions.reason: As French Judges 17:5 and 1 Samuel 15:23; Readable follows the English "household idols".

source.text: בִּֽימִינ֞וֹ הָיָ֣ה׀הַקֶּ֣סֶם יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם לָשׂ֤וּם כָּרִים֙ לִפְתֹּ֤חַ פֶּה֙ בְּרֶ֔צַח לְהָרִ֥ים ק֖וֹל בִּתְרוּעָ֑ה לָשׂ֤וּם כָּרִים֙ עַל־שְׁעָרִ֔ים לִשְׁפֹּ֥ךְ סֹלְלָ֖ה לִבְנ֥וֹת דָּיֵֽק׃

records.literal_gloss: Into his right hand comes the divination, Jerusalem: to set battering rams, to open [the] mouth with slaughter, to raise [the] voice with [a] battle cry, to set battering rams against [the] gates, to pour out a ramp, to build a siege wall.

en.L: Into his right hand has come the divination: Jerusalem! To set battering rams, to open the mouth with slaughter, to raise the voice with a battle cry, to set battering rams against the gates, to pour out a siege ramp, to build a siege wall.
en.B: The omen for Jerusalem falls into his right hand: to set up battering rams, to give the order to kill, to raise the battle cry, to set battering rams against the gates, to heap up a ramp and to build a siege wall.
en.R: The sign in his right hand points to Jerusalem. It tells him to set up battering rams, to shout the order to kill and to raise the war cry. He is to set battering rams against the city gates, pile up dirt ramps against the walls and build siege walls.

fr.L: Dans sa main droite est venue la divination : Jérusalem ! Pour placer des béliers, pour ouvrir la bouche au massacre, pour élever la voix avec un cri de guerre, pour placer des béliers contre les portes, pour verser une rampe, pour bâtir un mur de siège.
fr.B: Le présage pour Jérusalem tombe dans sa main droite : dresser des béliers, donner l’ordre de tuer, pousser le cri de guerre, dresser des béliers contre les portes, élever une rampe et construire un mur de siège.
fr.R: Le signe dans sa main droite indique Jérusalem. Il lui dit de dresser des béliers, de crier l’ordre de tuer et de pousser le cri de guerre. Il doit dresser des béliers contre les portes de la ville, entasser de la terre contre les murailles et construire des murs de siège.

es.L: En su mano derecha ha venido la adivinación: ¡Jerusalén! Para poner arietes, para abrir la boca con matanza, para alzar la voz con grito de guerra, para poner arietes contra las puertas, para levantar terraplén, para edificar muro de asedio.
es.B: En su mano derecha cae el presagio para Jerusalén: colocar arietes, dar la orden de matar, lanzar el grito de guerra, poner arietes contra las puertas, levantar un terraplén y construir un muro de asedio.
es.R: La señal que tiene en su mano derecha apunta a Jerusalén. Le dice que coloque arietes, que grite la orden de matar y que lance el grito de guerra. Debe poner arietes contra las puertas de la ciudad, amontonar tierra contra las murallas y construir muros de asedio.

decisions.choice: into his right hand comes the omen: the arrow marked "Jerusalem" is drawn
decisions.reason: The king draws the arrow with his right hand, and it bears the name of Jerusalem. The choice of road is made for him, and through it, the text implies, by the LORD.

decisions.choice: to open the mouth with slaughter: to give the order to kill
decisions.reason: To open the mouth is to speak; here the command to slaughter. Some ancient versions read "with a shout".

decisions.choice: battering rams, a siege ramp, a siege wall: the ways of besieging a city
decisions.reason: The same list is used in 4:2 for the siege Ezekiel acts out. Earth was heaped up against the walls so that the rams could reach them, and a wall or line of towers was built around the city to cut it off.

decisions.choice: to give the order to kill
alternatives: to open the mouth with slaughter
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the idiom means (m2).

source.text: וְהָיָ֨ה לָהֶ֤ם כִּקְסָם־שָׁוְא֙ בְּעֵ֣ינֵיהֶ֔ם שְׁבֻעֵ֥י שְׁבֻע֖וֹת לָהֶ֑ם וְהֽוּא־מַזְכִּ֥יר עָוֺ֖ן לְהִתָּפֵֽשׂ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And it will be to them like divination false in their eyes; oaths of oaths [are] theirs; but he brings to remembrance iniquity, to be captured.

en.L: And it will be to them like a false divination in their eyes; they have oaths sworn to them; but he brings [their] guilt to remembrance, so that they will be captured.
en.B: To the people of Jerusalem it will seem a false omen, since they have sworn solemn oaths. But he will bring their guilt to mind, and they will be captured.
en.R: To the people of Jerusalem it will look like a false sign, because they have sworn solemn oaths. But the king of Babylon will remember their guilt, and they will be captured.

fr.L: Et ce sera pour eux comme une divination mensongère à leurs yeux ; des serments de serments [sont] à eux ; mais lui rappelle la faute, pour qu’ils soient pris.
fr.B: Aux yeux des habitants de Jérusalem, ce sera un faux présage, puisqu’ils ont prêté des serments solennels. Mais lui rappellera leur faute, et ils seront pris.
fr.R: Pour les habitants de Jérusalem, ce sera un faux signe, parce qu’ils ont prêté des serments solennels. Mais le roi de Babylone se souviendra de leur faute, et ils seront faits prisonniers.

es.L: Y será para ellos como adivinación falsa a sus ojos; juramentos de juramentos tienen; pero él trae a la memoria la culpa, para que sean apresados.
es.B: A la gente de Jerusalén le parecerá un presagio falso, porque han hecho juramentos solemnes. Pero él les traerá a la memoria su culpa, y serán apresados.
es.R: A la gente de Jerusalén le parecerá una señal falsa, porque han hecho juramentos solemnes. Pero el rey de Babilonia recordará su culpa, y los tomará presos.

decisions.choice: they have sworn solemn oaths: the oaths of loyalty Judah swore to Babylon
alternatives: "they have the most solemn oaths", meaning God's promises, which they trust to protect them
the oaths their own diviners swore that the city would be safe
decisions.reason: The Hebrew, "oaths of oaths to them", is very compressed. The most likely sense is that the people of Jerusalem trusted the solemn oaths they had sworn, either to Babylon or to one another, so that they thought the omen could not be true. Zedekiah had sworn loyalty to Nebuchadnezzar and broken his oath (17:13-19).

decisions.choice: he brings guilt to remembrance: the king of Babylon calls their guilt to account
decisions.reason: "He" is most likely the king of Babylon, who will remember the broken oath and punish the rebellion. In the end it is also God's judgment (verse 29). "Bring guilt to remembrance" is legal language for calling a wrong to account (Numbers 5:15).

decisions.choice: the king of Babylon
decisions.reason: Readable names the one who remembers (m2).

source.text: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה־אָמַר֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ יַ֗עַן הַזְכַּרְכֶם֙ עֲוֺ֣נְכֶ֔ם בְּהִגָּל֣וֹת פִּשְׁעֵיכֶ֗ם לְהֵֽרָאוֹת֙ חַטֹּ֣אותֵיכֶ֔ם בְּכֹ֖ל עֲלִילֽוֹתֵיכֶ֑ם יַ֚עַן הִזָּ֣כֶרְכֶ֔ם בַּכַּ֖ף תִּתָּפֵֽשׂוּ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Therefore thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Because you have caused to be remembered your guilt, in [that] your transgressions are uncovered, so that your sins appear in all your deeds; because you have been remembered, by the hand you will be seized.

en.L: Therefore thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Because you have brought your guilt to remembrance, in that your transgressions are uncovered, so that your sins appear in all your deeds; because you have come to remembrance, you will be seized by the hand.
en.B: Therefore the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: You have brought your guilt to mind by your open rebellion, so that your sins show in everything you do. Because you have been called to account, you will be taken captive.
en.R: So this is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: You have made everyone remember your guilt. Your rebellion is out in the open, and your sins show in everything you do. Because of this, you will be called to account and taken prisoner.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi ainsi parle le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} : Parce que vous avez rappelé votre faute, en ce que vos transgressions sont mises à nu, de sorte que vos péchés apparaissent dans toutes vos actions ; parce que vous vous êtes rappelés [à la mémoire], vous serez saisis par la main.
fr.B: C’est pourquoi le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} dit ceci : Vous avez rappelé votre faute par vos crimes étalés au grand jour, si bien que vos péchés se voient dans tout ce que vous faites. Puisque vous êtes appelés à rendre des comptes, vous serez faits captifs.
fr.R: Alors voici ce que dit le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} : Vous avez fait que tout le monde se souvienne de votre faute. Votre révolte se voit au grand jour, et vos péchés se voient dans tout ce que vous faites. À cause de cela, vous devrez rendre des comptes, et vous serez faits prisonniers.

es.L: Por tanto, así dice el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}: Por cuanto {{plural_you:han hecho|habéis hecho}} recordar {{plural_you:su culpa|vuestra culpa}}, al quedar al descubierto {{plural_you:sus transgresiones|vuestras transgresiones}}, de manera que se ven {{plural_you:sus pecados|vuestros pecados}} en todas {{plural_you:sus obras|vuestras obras}}; por cuanto {{plural_you:han sido traídos|habéis sido traídos}} a la memoria, con la mano {{plural_you:serán apresados|seréis apresados}}.
es.B: Por eso el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}} dice esto: {{plural_you:Han hecho recordar su culpa con su rebelión|Habéis hecho recordar vuestra culpa con vuestra rebelión}} abierta, de manera que {{plural_you:sus pecados|vuestros pecados}} se ven en todo lo que {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}}. Por cuanto {{plural_you:han sido llamados|habéis sido llamados}} a cuentas, {{plural_you:serán llevados|seréis llevados}} cautivos.
es.R: Así que esto es lo que dice el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}: {{plural_you:Han hecho|Habéis hecho}} que todos recuerden {{plural_you:su culpa|vuestra culpa}}. {{plural_you:Su rebelión|Vuestra rebelión}} está a la vista de todos, y {{plural_you:sus pecados|vuestros pecados}} se ven en todo lo que {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}}. Por eso {{plural_you:tendrán|tendréis}} que rendir cuentas y {{plural_you:serán llevados|seréis llevados}} presos.

decisions.choice: remembered: called to account, a play on verse 28
decisions.reason: The verb "remember" runs through verses 28-29 and 37. The people's guilt is "remembered", brought before the judge; they themselves have "been remembered", called to account. In verse 37 Ammon "will not be remembered" at all.

decisions.choice: seized by the hand: taken captive
decisions.reason: To be taken "by the hand" is to fall into an enemy's power.

decisions.choice: transgressions (L); rebellion (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word for transgression follows the wording settled for the prophets: "transgression" (L), "rebellion" (B), "sin" (R). Readable uses "rebellion" here so that it is not the same word as the "sins" that follow.

decisions.choice: transgresiones (L); rebelión (B, R)
decisions.reason: Pesha' is 'transgresión' at L; here B and R use 'rebelión', as the English does, because the open revolt against Babylon is meant.

decisions.choice: *pesha'* "transgressions" (L), "crimes" (B), "révolte" (R), for the whole book
decisions.reason: The settled French ladder for *pesha'* in the prophets; Readable "révolte" follows the English "rebellion" here.

source.text: וְאַתָּה֙ חָלָ֣ל רָשָׁ֔ע נְשִׂ֖יא יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֣א יוֹמ֔וֹ בְּעֵ֖ת עֲוֺ֥ן קֵֽץ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And you, profane, wicked, prince of Israel, whose day has come, in [the] time of [the] iniquity of [the] end,

en.L: And you, profane [and] wicked one, prince of Israel, whose day has arrived, in the time of the punishment of the end,
en.B: As for you, profane and wicked prince of Israel, your day has come, the time of final punishment.
en.R: And you, wicked ruler of Israel, who has treated holy things with contempt, your day has come. It is the time of your final punishment.

fr.L: Et toi, profanateur [et] méchant, prince d’Israël, dont le jour est arrivé, au temps du châtiment de la fin,
fr.B: Quant à toi, prince d’Israël, profanateur et méchant, ton jour est arrivé, le temps du châtiment final.
fr.R: Et toi, chef méchant d’Israël, qui as traité avec mépris ce qui est saint, ton jour est arrivé. C’est le temps de ta punition finale.

es.L: Y tú, profano [y] malvado, príncipe de Israel, cuyo día ha llegado, en el tiempo de la culpa del fin,
es.B: En cuanto a ti, profano y malvado príncipe de Israel, ha llegado tu día, el tiempo del castigo final.
es.R: Y tú, malvado gobernante de Israel, que has tratado con desprecio las cosas santas, ha llegado tu día. Es el tiempo de tu castigo final.

decisions.choice: the prince of Israel: King Zedekiah
decisions.reason: Ezekiel calls Zedekiah "the prince" (12:10, 12) and does not use the word "king" for him. Zedekiah had broken his oath to Babylon (17:15-19) and, after the city fell, was blinded and taken to Babylon (2 Kings 25:6-7).

decisions.choice: profane: one who has treated holy things as common
alternatives: "pierced" or "slain", as the same word means in verses 19 and 34
decisions.reason: The word can mean "profane" or "pierced, slain". Zedekiah was not killed in battle, so "profane" fits him better here; but the play with the slain of the sword in the song is clear.

decisions.choice: the time of the iniquity of the end: the time when guilt brings final punishment
decisions.reason: The word for iniquity can mean guilt and also the punishment it brings. The same phrase is used in 21:34 and 35:5.

decisions.choice: who has treated holy things with contempt; ruler
decisions.reason: Readable says what "profane" means (m2), and uses "ruler" for "prince", as set for Ezekiel. The comma at Literal shows that the address runs on into the commands of verse 31.

source.text: כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה הָסִיר֙ הַמִּצְנֶ֔פֶת וְהָרִ֖ים הָֽעֲטָרָ֑ה זֹ֣את לֹא־זֹ֔את הַשָּׁפָ֣לָה הַגְבֵּ֔הַוְהַגָּבֹ֖הַהַשְׁפִּֽיל׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Remove the turban, and take off the crown! This [is] not this. The low exalt, and the high bring low.

en.L: Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Take off the turban, and remove the crown! This [will] not [be] this. Exalt the low, and bring low the high.
en.B: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: Take away the turban and lift off the crown! Things will not stay as they are. Raise up the low and bring down the high.
en.R: This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: Take off the king's turban, and remove his crown. Nothing will stay as it is. Lift up those who are low, and bring down those who are high.

fr.L: Ainsi parle le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} : Ôte le turban, et enlève la couronne ! Ceci ne [sera] pas ceci. Élève ce qui est bas, et abaisse ce qui est élevé.
fr.B: Le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} dit ceci : Retire le turban et enlève la couronne ! Les choses ne resteront pas comme elles sont. Élève ce qui est bas et abaisse ce qui est élevé.
fr.R: Voici ce que dit le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} : Enlève le turban du roi, et retire sa couronne. Rien ne restera comme avant. Élève ceux qui sont en bas, et abaisse ceux qui sont en haut.

es.L: Así dice el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}: ¡Quita el turbante y depón la corona! Esto no [será] esto. Exalta lo bajo y abate lo alto.
es.B: El Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}} dice esto: ¡Quítate el turbante y despójate de la corona! Las cosas no seguirán como están. Levanta al humilde y derriba al altivo.
es.R: Esto es lo que dice el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}: Quítale al rey su turbante y su corona. Nada seguirá como está. Levanta a los de abajo y derriba a los de arriba.

decisions.choice: the turban and the crown: signs of rule
alternatives: the high priest's turban, so that priesthood and kingship both end
decisions.reason: The word for turban is used elsewhere for the high priest's headdress (Exodus 28:4, 37), but here it stands beside the crown as a sign of the ruler's office. Some take it to mean that both the priestly and the royal offices come to an end with Jerusalem's fall.

decisions.choice: this is not this: things will not remain as they are
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is a short saying, literally "this not this". It means that the present order is about to be overturned, as the next words say.

decisions.choice: exalt the low, bring low the high: God overturns the powerful
decisions.reason: The same reversal is sung by Hannah (1 Samuel 2:7-8) and by Mary (Luke 1:52), and Ezekiel uses it of the trees in 17:24.

decisions.choice: the king's turban; his crown
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain whose turban and crown are meant (verse 30).

decisions.choice: ¡Quítate el turbante y despójate de la corona!
alternatives: ¡Quita el turbante y retira la corona!
decisions.reason: The order is read at B as spoken to the prince of verse 30, who takes off the signs of his rule; L keeps the plain verbs and R names the king, as the English R does.

source.text: עַוָּ֥ה עַוָּ֖ה עַוָּ֣ה אֲשִׂימֶ֑נָּה גַּם־זֹאת֙ לֹ֣א הָיָ֔ה עַד־בֹּ֛א אֲשֶׁר־ל֥וֹ הַמִּשְׁפָּ֖ט וּנְתַתִּֽיו׃פ

records.literal_gloss: A ruin, a ruin, a ruin I will make it; also this not will be, until comes [he] whom to him [is] the judgment, and I will give it.

en.L: A ruin, a ruin, a ruin I will make it! This also will not be, until he comes to whom the judgment [belongs], and I will give it [to him].
en.B: A ruin, a ruin, a ruin I will make it! Even this will be no more, until he comes to whom the right belongs, and I will give it to him.
en.R: I will make it a ruin, a ruin, a ruin! It will be gone until the one comes who has the right to it. I will give it to him.

fr.L: Une ruine, une ruine, une ruine, j’en ferai ! Cela non plus ne sera plus, jusqu’à ce que vienne celui à qui [appartient] le jugement, et je le [lui] donnerai.
fr.B: J’en ferai une ruine, une ruine, une ruine ! Même cela ne sera plus, jusqu’à ce que vienne celui à qui appartient le droit, et je le lui donnerai.
fr.R: J’en ferai une ruine, une ruine, une ruine ! Il n’en restera rien jusqu’à ce que vienne celui qui y a droit. Je le lui donnerai.

es.L: ¡Ruina, ruina, ruina la haré! También esto no será, hasta que venga aquel a quien [pertenece] el derecho, y se lo daré.
es.B: ¡Ruina, ruina, ruina la haré! Y aun esto dejará de existir, hasta que venga aquel a quien le corresponde el derecho, y yo se lo daré.
es.R: ¡La haré una ruina, una ruina, una ruina! Desaparecerá hasta que venga aquel que tiene derecho a ella. Yo se la daré.

decisions.choice: until he comes to whom it belongs: an echo of Genesis 49:10
alternatives: the one to whom judgment is given, meaning Nebuchadnezzar, who will carry out God's judgment on Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The words recall Jacob's blessing of Judah: "the scepter shall not depart from Judah ... until he comes to whom it belongs" (Genesis 49:10, as many read it). Here the kingship is overturned and left in ruins until the rightful one comes; Ezekiel speaks later of a coming shepherd-king from David's line (34:23-24; 37:24). The word translated "right" also means "judgment", and some take the verse to mean the one appointed to carry out judgment. Later Jewish and Christian readers took the verse as a promise of the Messiah. The text does not name him.

decisions.choice: a ruin, a ruin, a ruin: the threefold word for complete overthrow
decisions.reason: Repeating a word three times makes it as strong as Hebrew can, as in "holy, holy, holy" (Isaiah 6:3). What will be ruined is the kingship of verse 31.

decisions.choice: the right (B); the right to it (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the word chosen in m1; Literal keeps "the judgment". The one who comes is not named, so no pronoun for him takes the capitalized setting.

source.text: וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן־אָדָ֗ם הִנָּבֵ֤א וְאָֽמַרְתָּ֙ כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֔ה אֶל־בְּנֵ֥י עַמּ֖וֹן וְאֶל־חֶרְפָּתָ֑ם וְאָמַרְתָּ֗ חֶ֣רֶב חֶ֤רֶב פְּתוּחָה֙ לְטֶ֣בַח מְרוּטָ֔ה לְהָכִ֖יל לְמַ֥עַן בָּרָֽק׃

records.literal_gloss: And you, son of man, prophesy and say, Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh concerning [the] sons of Ammon and concerning their reproach; and say, A sword, a sword drawn, for slaughter polished, to consume, in order to [be] lightning,

en.L: And you, son of man, prophesy and say, Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} concerning the {{gender:children|sons}} of Ammon and concerning their taunting; and say: A sword, a sword is drawn, polished for slaughter, to consume, so as to be like lightning,
en.B: And you, son of man, prophesy and say, The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this about the Ammonites and their taunts. Say: A sword, a sword is drawn for slaughter, polished to devour and to flash like lightning,
en.R: Son of man, prophesy. Say, This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says about the Ammonites, who mock Israel: A sword, a sword is drawn to kill! It is polished to destroy and to flash like lightning.

fr.L: Et toi, fils d’homme, prophétise et dis : Ainsi parle le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} au sujet des {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Ammon et au sujet de leurs insultes ; et dis : Une épée, une épée est tirée, polie pour le massacre, pour dévorer, pour être comme l’éclair,
fr.B: Et toi, fils d’homme, prophétise et dis : Le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} dit ceci au sujet des Ammonites et de leurs insultes. Dis : L’épée, l’épée est tirée pour le massacre, polie pour dévorer et pour briller comme l’éclair,
fr.R: Fils d’homme, prophétise. Dis : Voici ce que dit le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} au sujet des Ammonites, qui se moquent d’Israël : Une épée, une épée est tirée pour tuer ! Elle est polie pour détruire et pour briller comme l’éclair.

es.L: Y tú, hijo de hombre, profetiza y di: Así dice el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}} acerca de los hijos de Amón y acerca de su afrenta; y di: ¡Una espada, una espada está desenvainada, pulida para la matanza, para consumir, para ser como relámpago!,
es.B: Y tú, hijo de hombre, profetiza y di: El Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}} dice esto acerca de los amonitas y de sus burlas. Di: Una espada, una espada está desenvainada para la matanza, pulida para devorar y para brillar como relámpago,
es.R: Hijo de hombre, profetiza. Di: Esto es lo que dice el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}} acerca de los amonitas, que se burlan de Israel: ¡Una espada, una espada está desenvainada para matar! Está pulida para destruir y para brillar como relámpago.

decisions.choice: the Ammonites and their taunting: Ammon mocked Judah's fall
decisions.reason: Ammon rejoiced over the ruin of the temple and the land (25:3, 6). Zephaniah 2:8 also speaks of the "taunts" of the Ammonites. Though the king of Babylon chose Jerusalem first (verse 27), Ammon will not escape.

decisions.choice: a sword, a sword: the song of verses 14-15 taken up again
decisions.reason: The words of the sword song return, now turned against Ammon.

decisions.choice: who mock Israel
decisions.reason: Readable says whom the Ammonites taunted. The comma at Literal and Balanced shows that the sentence runs on into verse 34.

source.text: בַּחֲז֥וֹת לָךְ֙ שָׁ֔וְא בִּקְסָם־לָ֖ךְ כָּזָ֑ב לָתֵ֣ת אוֹתָ֗ךְ אֶֽל־צַוְּארֵי֙ חַֽלְלֵ֣י רְשָׁעִ֔ים אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֣א יוֹמָ֔ם בְּעֵ֖ת עֲוֺ֥ן קֵֽץ׃

records.literal_gloss: while they see for you worthless [visions], while they divine for you a lie, to put you on [the] necks of [the] slain wicked ones, whose day has come, in [the] time of [the] iniquity of [the] end.

en.L: while they see empty visions for you, while they divine lies for you, to lay you on the necks of the slain, the wicked, whose day has arrived, in the time of the punishment of the end.
en.B: while they see false visions for you and divine lies for you, to lay you on the necks of the slain, the wicked, whose day has arrived, the time of their final punishment.
en.R: False prophets see visions for you that mean nothing and tell lies about the future. But the sword will be laid on the necks of the wicked who are to be killed. Their day has come, the time of their final punishment.

fr.L: pendant qu’on a pour toi des visions vaines, pendant qu’on pratique pour toi la divination de mensonge, pour te poser sur les cous des tués, des méchants, dont le jour est arrivé, au temps du châtiment de la fin.
fr.B: pendant qu’on a pour toi des visions fausses et qu’on pratique pour toi une divination mensongère, pour te poser sur le cou des tués, des méchants, dont le jour est arrivé, le temps de leur châtiment final.
fr.R: De faux prophètes ont des visions qui ne valent rien et disent des mensonges sur l’avenir. Mais l’épée sera posée sur le cou des méchants qui doivent être tués. Leur jour est arrivé, le temps de leur punition finale.

es.L: mientras ven para ti visiones vanas, mientras adivinan para ti mentira, para ponerte sobre los cuellos de los muertos, de los malvados, cuyo día ha llegado, en el tiempo de la culpa del fin.
es.B: mientras ven para ti visiones falsas y adivinan para ti mentiras, para ponerte sobre el cuello de los que han de morir, de los malvados, cuyo día ha llegado, el tiempo de su castigo final.
es.R: Los falsos profetas ven para ti visiones que no significan nada y dicen mentiras sobre el futuro. Pero la espada caerá sobre el cuello de los malvados que han de morir. Ha llegado su día, el tiempo de su castigo final.

decisions.choice: "you" here is the sword, laid on the necks of the wicked; false prophets promise safety
alternatives: "you" is Ammon, whose diviners deceive it, and which will be laid among the slain
decisions.reason: The "you" is feminine in Hebrew, like the word "sword". The sword is laid on the necks of the wicked while the diviners offer false comfort. The same "you" in verses 35-37 is then most likely Ammon (see verse 35). The verses are hard, and who is addressed is not certain.

decisions.choice: the slain: the same word as "profane" in verse 30
decisions.reason: Here the plural clearly means people killed by the sword, and with "the wicked" it echoes the description of Zedekiah in verse 30.

decisions.choice: false prophets ...; the sword will be laid on the necks
alternatives: they see ... for you; to lay you on the necks
decisions.reason: Readable names those who see false visions, and says "the sword" for the feminine "you", following m1.

decisions.choice: ti / ponerte, singular, for the sword
decisions.reason: The 'you' of this verse is the sword (feminine singular in Spanish as in Hebrew), so the forms are singular 'tú'.

source.text: הָשַׁ֖ב אֶל־תַּעְרָ֑הּ בִּמְק֧וֹם אֲשֶׁר־נִבְרֵ֛את בְּאֶ֥רֶץ מְכֻרוֹתַ֖יִךְ אֶשְׁפֹּ֥ט אֹתָֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: Return [it] to its sheath! In [the] place where you were created, in [the] land of your origin, I will judge you.

en.L: Return [it] to its sheath! In the place in which you were created, in the land of your origins, I will judge you.
en.B: Put the sword back in its sheath! Where you were created, in the land of your birth, there I will judge you.
en.R: Put the sword back into its sheath! I will judge you in the place where you were made, in the land where you began.

fr.L: Remets[-la] dans son fourreau ! Au lieu de ta création, dans le pays de tes origines, je te jugerai.
fr.B: Remets l’épée dans son fourreau ! Là où tu as pris naissance, dans le pays de ton origine, là je te jugerai.
fr.R: Remets l’épée dans son fourreau ! Je te jugerai à l’endroit où tu as commencé à exister, dans le pays de tes origines.

es.L: ¡Vuelve[la] a su vaina! En el lugar de tu creación, en la tierra de tu origen, te juzgaré.
es.B: ¡Vuelve la espada a su vaina! Allí donde tuviste tu origen, en la tierra donde naciste, allí te juzgaré.
es.R: ¡Vuelve a guardar la espada en su vaina! Te juzgaré en el lugar donde comenzaste, en la tierra donde naciste.

decisions.choice: the one addressed is Ammon: it will be judged in its own land
alternatives: Babylon, God's sword, which will itself be judged in its own land once its work is done (as Jeremiah 50-51)
decisions.reason: After the sword has done its work, the one addressed is told to put it away and is judged "in the land of your origin". Ammon fits this, since verse 37 says "you will not be remembered", as 25:10 says of Ammon. Some take the verses as a word against Babylon, the sword of God, which will in turn be judged.

decisions.choice: the sword
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no object for "return"; the sheath shows that the sword is meant.

source.text: וְשָׁפַכְתִּ֤י עָלַ֨יִךְ֙ זַעְמִ֔י בְּאֵ֥שׁ עֶבְרָתִ֖י אָפִ֣יחַ עָלָ֑יִךְ וּנְתַתִּ֗יךְ בְּיַד֙ אֲנָשִׁ֣ים בֹּֽעֲרִ֔ים חָרָשֵׁ֖י מַשְׁחִֽית׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will pour out on you my indignation; with [the] fire of my wrath I will blow on you, and I will give you into [the] hand of men brutal, craftsmen of destruction.

en.L: And I will pour out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} indignation on you; with the fire of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath I will blow on you, and I will give you into the hand of brutal men, craftsmen of destruction.
en.B: I will pour out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} indignation on you and blow on you with the fire of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath. I will hand you over to brutal men, skilled at destroying.
en.R: I will pour out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger on you. I will breathe out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} fiery anger against you. I will hand you over to cruel men who are experts at destroying.

fr.L: Et je répandrai sur toi {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} indignation ; du feu de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} fureur je soufflerai sur toi, et je te livrerai entre les mains d’hommes brutaux, artisans de destruction.
fr.B: Je répandrai sur toi {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} indignation et je soufflerai sur toi le feu de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} fureur. Je te livrerai à des hommes brutaux, habiles à détruire.
fr.R: Je répandrai {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} colère sur toi. Je soufflerai sur toi le feu de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} colère. Je te livrerai à des hommes cruels, experts dans l’art de détruire.

es.L: Y derramaré sobre ti {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} indignación; con el fuego de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} furor soplaré sobre ti, y te entregaré en mano de hombres brutales, artífices de destrucción.
es.B: Derramaré sobre ti {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} indignación y soplaré sobre ti con el fuego de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} furor. Te entregaré a hombres brutales, expertos en destruir.
es.R: Derramaré sobre ti {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} enojo. Soplaré contra ti el fuego de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} enojo. Te entregaré a hombres crueles que saben destruir muy bien.

decisions.choice: blow on you with the fire of my wrath: like a smith blowing on a forge
decisions.reason: The picture is of air blown on a fire to make it hotter. Ezekiel uses it at length for Jerusalem in 22:20-21.

decisions.choice: brutal men, craftsmen of destruction
decisions.reason: The first word is used of senseless, brutish people (Psalm 92:7). The second, "craftsmen" or "smiths", fits the forge of the first half: the one who was "created" (verse 35) is handed over to men skilled only in destroying.

source.text: לָאֵ֤שׁ תִּֽהְיֶה֙ לְאָכְלָ֔ה דָּמֵ֥ךְ יִהְיֶ֖ה בְּת֣וֹךְ הָאָ֑רֶץ לֹ֣א תִזָּכֵ֔רִי כִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבַּֽרְתִּי׃פ

records.literal_gloss: For the fire you will be fuel; your blood will be in [the] midst of the land; not will you be remembered, for I, Yahweh, have spoken.

en.L: You will be fuel for the fire; your blood will be in the midst of the land; you will be remembered no more, for I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have spoken.
en.B: You will be fuel for the fire, and your blood will be spilled in the land. You will be remembered no more, for I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have spoken.
en.R: You will be burned up like wood in a fire. Your blood will be spilled in your land. No one will remember you, because I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have spoken.

fr.L: Pour le feu tu seras du combustible ; ton sang sera au milieu du pays ; on ne se souviendra plus de toi, car moi, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, j’ai parlé.
fr.B: Tu serviras de combustible au feu, et ton sang sera répandu dans le pays. On ne se souviendra plus de toi, car moi, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, j’ai parlé.
fr.R: Tu brûleras comme du bois dans le feu. Ton sang sera répandu dans ton pays. Personne ne se souviendra de toi, parce que c’est moi, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, qui le dis.

es.L: Para el fuego serás pasto; tu sangre estará en medio de la tierra; no serás recordado más, porque yo, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, he hablado.
es.B: Serás pasto del fuego, y tu sangre se derramará en la tierra. No serás recordado más, porque yo, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, he hablado.
es.R: Te quemarás como leña en el fuego. Tu sangre se derramará en tu tierra. Nadie se acordará de ti, porque yo, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, lo he dicho.

decisions.choice: you will not be remembered: a people that will vanish from memory
decisions.reason: The same words are said of Ammon in 25:10. To be forgotten was the end of a people's name and life.

decisions.choice: I, the LORD, have spoken: the closing seal
decisions.reason: The chapter ends as the sword song did (verse 22).

decisions.choice: spilled
alternatives: your blood will be in the midst of the land
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what blood "in the land" means.
